sentences.text:
This first application has been filed by applicant under Section 483 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 for grant of bail in connection with Crime No.991/2024 registered at Police Station,
Chandan Nagar District Indore (MP) for offence punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471, 201 of IPC

entities.text:
Police Station,
Chandan Nagar District Indore
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The applicant is in custody since 7.11.2024.

As per the case of prosecution, Khalil Unnabi (applicant) has forged an agreement to sale for consideration of Rs. 39,83,71600/- with regard to transfer of immovable property by impersonating Simmi Bahal, title holder of the land.
He attempted to transfer the land to Harish Sahu on the basis of such forged agreement to sale.
P.S. Chandan Nagar registered FIR for offence punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468 and NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:6859 2 MCRC-9076-2025 471 of IPC against Khalil Unnabi.
The statements of witnesses were recorded.
On completion of investigation, final report was submitted.
Learned counsel for the applicant in addition to the grounds mentioned in the application submits that the applicant has been falsely implicated in this matter.
No offence, as alleged, is committed by the applicant.
The transaction involved is civil in nature.

The complainant declined to perform the contract and false prosecution is lodged against the applicant to pressurize him for settlement in Khalil Unnabi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168188463/

sentences.text: Learned counsel referring to the civil suit and other proceedings pending before the Court of Principal District Judge Indore submits that the parties are under litigation on civil side.

entities.text: Court of Principal District Judge Indore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The applicant is respectable citizen.
The trial would take time to conclude.
Therefore, the applicant may be extended benefit of bail.
Per contra, learned counsel for the State ably assisted by the counsel for the objector opposes the bail application on the ground of gravity of alleged offence.

Referring to the statements on record,
learned counsel submits that even the witness of execution of agreement to sale have denied execution of agreement by land owner Simmi Bahel in their presence.
No amount as stated in the agreement was paid to the complainant/title holder Simmi Bahel.
Harish Sahu, the subsequent purchaser, has specifically alleged cheating by applicant.
Further, criminal antecedent of one similar case is reported by concerned police station.
Therefore, the applicant may not be extended benefit of bail.

NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:6859 3 MCRC-9076-2025 Heard the arguments,
perused the grounds for grant of bail stated in the application and the case diary.
The case diary and the material on record reveal that allegedly the applicant has forged the agreement to sale and attempted to transfer the property to Harish Sahu.
The complainant and Harish Sahu have made specific allegation of cheating and forgery against the applicant.
Mere pendency of the civil litigation between the parties is not sufficient to exonerate the applicant of the allegations.
The original agreement to sale could not be recovered during investigation.
Considering the conduct and circumstances as reflected by material on record, the possibility of tampering with evidence cannot be ruled out.
In view of the specific allegation, overall circumstances of the case, this Court is of the considered view that the applicant does not deserve to be released on bail.
Present bail application (MCRC No. 9076 of 2025) stands dismissed accordingly.

(SANJEEV S KALGAONKAR) JUDGE BDJ NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:6859 4 MCRC-9076-2025 Khalil Unnabi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168188463/
